title: Grateful Dead Live at Metropolitan Sports Center on 1973-10-23

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording captures a jazzy late‑'73 show highlighted by Keith’s rare organ on Truckin’ and an energetic Other One, with Bill’s drums front‑and‑center; occasional clipping but overall good quality.
ai_review.review: The performance is praised for its creative jamming, especially the organ‑tinged Truckin’, a fire‑breathing Other One, and a hilariously confrontational Casey Jones that even includes Phil’s on‑stage heckling. The soundboard source is generally clear and showcases Bill Kreutzmann’s full‑range jazzy drumming, though listeners note occasional clipping and speaker crackle. Overall the show is regarded as a standout example of the late‑1973 Dead vibe.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars and highlight strong musical moments; only one low rating mentions clipping, so the combined show (70%) and recording (30%) assessment lands in the good‑to‑great range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and well‑balanced with a strong Wall of Sound mix, but several listeners report occasional clipping levels and speaker cracking during the tape.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A typical late‑'73 set with jazzy improvisation; the first encore was interrupted by security, leading to a memorable onstage confrontation that adds humor and energy.

band_member_comments.Phil: His outspoken reaction to a security guard during Casey Jones is noted as funny and adds character to the performance.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s unusual organ work (heard on Truckin’/Black‑Throated Wind) is highlighted as a rare, exciting moment that gives the show a primal ’69‑70 flavor.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drums are praised for being loud, full‑range and showcasing his 1973 jazzy style.
